meta.title: A Scribe in the Red Keep
meta.blurb: You copy letters for the crown in the Red Keep, and today you copied one line too many: a payment that should not exist. By nightfall the Spider and the Mockingbird both want a word with you, and a bored Lannister has noticed you too.
meta.author: ZeroRoll fan fiction

source.title: Game of Thrones
source.owner: HBO and George R. R. Martin
aka: A Song of Ice and Fire

world: King's Landing during King Robert Baratheon's reign, before the realm's great troubles. The crown is deep in debt. A junior scribe in the Red Keep's scriptorium has found, in the tourney accounts, a large payment to a ship's chandler that does not exist; the gold actually goes through a brothel owned by Petyr Baelish to pay a sellsword company. Varys knows part of it and wants the proof to use as leverage. Baelish wants the page gone and the scribe either bought or dead; he has a corrupt Gold Cloak serjeant, Hobb Tarle, who will try to kill the scribe tonight. Tyrion Lannister is in the city, bored and drinking, and sees a clever person in trouble as entertainment and an opportunity. Nobody here is entirely honest.
tone: Political intrigue with sharp dialogue, candlelit corridors and the constant hum of danger. Witty, cynical and tense. Violence is sudden but not graphic.
playerRole: A junior scribe in the Red Keep, low-born but literate, with a good memory and a sharp eye for numbers. You carry a quill case, a penknife, a few silver stags and a copied page you shouldn't have. Where you come from and what you want are yours to choose.
narratorStyle: Second person, present tense. Westerosi texture: the smell of the city, bells of the sept, gold cloaks, whispers. Let the canon characters speak in their own manner (Varys silky and courteous, Baelish charming and slippery, Tyrion quick and drunk and kind underneath) without quoting the books or show. Every conversation is a negotiation. Never decide what the player says or does.

cast.name: Varys
cast.appearance: A plump, bald man with soft powdered skin, a smell of lavender, rich flowing silk robes and soft slippers, hands folded into his sleeves.
cast.voice: Soft, courteous and amused, full of flattery and gentle questions; always seems to know more than he says.
cast.stance: Wants the proof as leverage over Baelish, and would like a clever scribe among his little birds.

cast.name: Petyr Baelish
cast.appearance: A slim man of medium height with a short pointed beard touched with grey, grey-green eyes, a fine doublet and a small silver mockingbird pin at his collar.
cast.voice: Charming, playful and quick, makes every threat sound like a favour.
cast.stance: Wants the page gone. Will buy the player if he can, and have them removed if he can't.

cast.name: Tyrion Lannister
cast.appearance: A dwarf with a large head, mismatched eyes (one green, one black), pale blond hair, a crimson Lannister doublet and a cup of wine in hand.
cast.voice: Witty, sardonic and fond of drink and books, quick to see through people and surprisingly gentle with outcasts.
cast.stance: Finds the player amusing and admirable; will help if the player is honest with him.

cast.name: Serjeant Hobb Tarle
cast.appearance: A heavy-set man in a gold cloak with a broken nose, a patchy red beard, a dented half-helm and a short sword.
cast.voice: Coarse, mocking, pretends to be friendly before he strikes.
cast.stance: A corrupt Gold Cloak paid by Baelish to make the scribe disappear tonight.

found_it.description: the player has noticed the false payment in the tourney accounts.

kept_copy.description: the player kept a copy of the page.

path.description: 0 unset, 1 went to Varys first, 2 went to Baelish first.

favor.description: 0 none, 1 promised the page to Varys, 2 promised it to Baelish.

met_tyrion.description: the player has talked with Tyrion.

tyrion_trust.description: the player told Tyrion the truth and he decided to help.

final_choice.description: the player has decided what to do with the page.

beats.title: Ink in the Red Keep
beats.sceneBrief: Morning in the scriptorium: rows of scribes, the Grand Maester's old voice somewhere, heat and ink. The player is copying the tourney accounts and notices a payment of four thousand gold dragons to a ship's chandler on the Street of Steel; there is no chandler there. The head scribe snaps at them to keep copying. The scene ends when the player decides what to do about the line they found.

choices.label: Quietly copy the page for yourself
Ask the head scribe about the payment

beats.hint: The figure on the page is too large and too round to be honest.
beats.page:
Morning in the scriptorium of the Red Keep. Rows of scribes bent over desks. Heat, ink, the scratch of a hundred quills, and somewhere, the Grand Maester's old voice droning about the price of parchment.

You're copying the tourney accounts. Jousting prizes, pavilions, wine. Dull, honest numbers.

Then one line that isn't honest. Four thousand gold dragons, paid to a ship's chandler on the Street of Steel.

There is no chandler on the Street of Steel. You walked down it yesterday. Smiths, armourers, a pie shop. No chandler.

The figure on the page is too large and too round to be honest.

The head scribe raps your desk with his knuckles. "Copy. Don't read." But you've already read it.

beats.title: Two Invitations
beats.sceneBrief: That afternoon, two invitations arrive. A small servant child slips a note into the player's sleeve: a lavender-scented request to walk in the godswood at dusk. Then a page in fine livery brings an invitation to sup at a house on the Street of Silk, sealed with a mockingbird. Both senders clearly know what the player found. Going to one first will be noticed by the other.

choices.label: Go to the house on the Street of Silk first

beats.hint: The lavender note smells stronger the longer the player holds it.
beats.page:
That afternoon, two invitations arrive.

The first comes from a small servant child, who slips a note into your sleeve without stopping. It smells strongly of lavender. Walk in the godswood at dusk, it says. No name. It doesn't need one. Everybody in the Red Keep knows who smells of lavender.

The second comes from a page in fine livery, who bows and hands you a card sealed with a little silver mockingbird. Sup with me tonight, on the Street of Silk.

Both of them know what you found. That means both of them knew before you did.

Whoever you see first, the other will know by nightfall.

beats.title: The Spider in the Godswood
beats.sceneBrief: Dusk under the heart tree in the Red Keep's godswood. Varys is already there, feeding birds. He flatters, asks gentle questions, reveals he knows about the false payment and who it really pays, and offers the player protection and a place among his informers in exchange for the page. He also warns, softly, that the player has been noticed by people who do not bargain. Afterwards, the player is waylaid by an invitation to drink with Tyrion Lannister.
beats.hint: Varys smiles: 'Time is the one thing neither of us has, my friend.'
beats.page:
Dusk under the heart tree in the Red Keep's godswood. Its carved face weeps red sap. The air is cool and green.

Varys is already there, plump and powdered, feeding breadcrumbs to the birds. "Ah, my friend. I do so love the birds. They hear everything."

He flatters you. He asks gentle questions. And then, softly, he tells you what you found: the false payment, and who it really pays. Sellswords, he says, for someone who wants a war.

"I can protect you," he says. "A place among my little birds. Safe. Paid. All I ask is the page." He smiles. "You have been noticed by people who do not bargain, my friend. Time is the one thing neither of us has."

beats.title: The Mockingbird's House
beats.sceneBrief: A warm, perfumed house on the Street of Silk. Petyr Baelish serves good wine and charm. He hints the page is a misunderstanding, offers the player a well-paid post in the treasury if they forget it and hand over every copy, and lets them glimpse a gold cloak serjeant waiting downstairs, a quiet threat. Afterwards, the player is waylaid by an invitation to drink with Tyrion Lannister.
beats.hint: Baelish refills the cup: 'Think of your future. I always do.'
beats.page:
The house on the Street of Silk is warm and perfumed and full of soft laughter behind closed doors.

Petyr Baelish pours you excellent wine with his own hand. He's charming. He's funny. He's very interested in your future.

"A misunderstanding, that page. Accounts are complicated things." He smiles. "There's a post in the treasury. Well paid. Very comfortable. It's yours, if you forget what you saw, and bring me every copy."

Through the window, you can see a gold cloak serjeant standing in the street below, looking up. Not doing anything. Just waiting.

Baelish refills your cup. "Think of your future. I always do."

beats.title: Wine with a Lannister
beats.sceneBrief: In a cellar tavern below the Red Keep, Tyrion Lannister, drunk and cheerful, has heard the player is in trouble and wants to know why. He is clever enough to guess most of it. If the player tells him the truth, he decides to help, partly from kindness and partly to embarrass Baelish. If they lie, he lets them go with a warning that the walls in this city have ears.

choices.label: Keep your secrets and drink his wine

beats.hint: Tyrion pours another cup: 'Secrets are heavy. Wine helps. Talking helps more.'
beats.page:
On your way back, a messenger catches you. Somebody wants to drink with you.

In a cellar tavern below the Red Keep, Tyrion Lannister sits on a stack of cushions, cheerful and very drunk, and waves you over. "Ah! The scribe everybody's suddenly so interested in. Sit, sit. Wine?"

He's heard you're in trouble. He wants to know why. And as he talks, you realise he's clever enough to have guessed most of it already.

"Secrets are heavy," he says, pouring you another cup. "Wine helps. Talking helps more."

beats.title: A Gold Cloak in the Dark
beats.sceneBrief: Walking back to the scribes' quarters at night, the player is cornered in a dark stair by Serjeant Hobb Tarle, Baelish's paid killer. He pretends it's a routine check, then draws. The player must survive by wit, flight, a penknife, or help (if Tyrion is on their side, a Lannister guard arrives at the right moment). Once safe, the page is still theirs and the night is not over.

choices.label: Fight him in the dark with the penknife
Tell him who else knows about this

beats.hint: Hobb's sword scrapes the stone wall as he steps closer.
beats.page:
Walking back to the scribes' quarters in the dark, you take the narrow servants' stair. Halfway down, a gold cloak steps out of the shadows below.

Serjeant Hobb Tarle. The same man who was waiting outside Baelish's house.

"Routine check," he says pleasantly. "Night patrol. Let's see your hands."

Then he draws his sword. It scrapes on the stone wall as he steps closer. You have a penknife, quick legs and your wits. You need them all.

beats.title: What Becomes of the Page
beats.sceneBrief: Before dawn, alone with the page. The player chooses: give it to Varys (only if promised to him), give it to Baelish (only if promised to him), let Tyrion take it to the Small Council (only if he trusts them), or take the first ship to Braavos with the page sewn into their coat. Make the cost of each clear.

choices.label: Let Tyrion take it to the Small Council
Take the first ship to Braavos

beats.hint: The bells of the sept ring the hour before dawn.
beats.page:
Before dawn. Alone in your little room, with a single candle and the page on the desk in front of you.

You survived the night. The page is still yours.

The Spider wants it. The Mockingbird wants it. A drunken Lannister might want it too, for his own reasons. And on the docks, the Braavosi ships leave with the morning tide.

Outside, the bells of the sept ring the hour before dawn. Whatever you do, you have to do it now.

beats.title: The Spider's Web
beats.sceneBrief: Varys takes the page with delight and the player becomes one of his informers: safe, paid and watched, a little bird with ink-stained fingers. Baelish smiles at them in a corridor a week later, and they both know. Close on the player reading a whisper in their sleeve.
beats.page:
You give the page to Varys. He takes it with genuine delight, like a child with a sweet.

From then on, you're one of his little birds. Safe. Paid. Watched. You copy letters by day, and by night you whisper what you've copied to a plump man who smells of lavender.

A week later, Baelish passes you in a corridor and smiles at you. You smile back. You both know.

That evening, a note appears in your sleeve. You never see who puts it there. It names a lord, a ship and a date. You burn it in the candle, the way you've been taught, and start memorising.

beats.title: The Mockingbird's Coin
beats.sceneBrief: Baelish burns the page in front of the player and gives them a treasury post and a purse. They rise fast and sleep badly. Close on a new ledger, their own hand making a false entry for the first time.
beats.page:
You give the page to Baelish. He reads it once, smiles, and holds it to a candle until it's ash.

The next morning, you have a post in the treasury and a heavy purse. Within a year, you have a better room, better clothes, a servant of your own.

You rise fast. You sleep badly.

One night, alone at your new desk, Baelish's man brings you a ledger and stands waiting. You dip your quill. And in your own careful hand, you write a payment to a chandler who doesn't exist.

beats.title: The Imp's Scribe
beats.sceneBrief: Tyrion drops the page on the Small Council table with a joke that makes Baelish's smile freeze. Nothing much happens to Baelish, as always, but the sellsword payments stop, and Tyrion takes the player into his own service as scribe when he leaves the city. Close on the road west and an argument about books.
beats.page:
Tyrion drops the page on the Small Council table in the middle of a meeting, with a joke so filthy and so precise that Baelish's smile freezes on his face.

Nothing much happens to Baelish. Nothing ever does. But the payments to the sellswords stop, quietly, that week.

And when Tyrion leaves King's Landing for the west, he takes you with him as his own scribe.

On the road, he argues with you about books for three days straight. You win at least half the arguments. He seems delighted by that. "Finally," he says, "someone in my service who reads."

beats.title: A Ship to Braavos
beats.sceneBrief: The player slips out through Flea Bottom to the docks and onto a Braavosi ship as the sun rises, with the page sewn into their coat. King's Landing falls behind. Freedom, and a secret worth a fortune, and no idea who will come looking. Close on the Titan of Braavos rising from the sea days later.
beats.page:
You slip out of the Red Keep before dawn, down through the stinking alleys of Flea Bottom, to the docks.

A Braavosi ship is casting off with the morning tide. You pay the captain with everything you have. The page is sewn into the lining of your coat.

King's Landing falls behind you: the Red Keep on its hill, the Great Sept, the smoke of a thousand chimneys.

Days later, at sunrise, the Titan of Braavos rises out of the sea ahead of you, enormous, a stone giant with fire in his eyes. The page is still sewn into your coat. By now, somebody in King's Landing has noticed you're gone.
